correctness.rationale: The eigenvalue probability law follows from polar integration: F_m(u)=2(m+1)u-(u_+)^alpha, with saddle u_m and curvature scale s_m. The phase identity -u_m^alpha[v^alpha-alpha v+(alpha-1)] establishes Gaussian L1 convergence with negligible negative half-line and tails; center spacing (u_(m+q)-u_m)/s_m=2qs_m(1+o(1)) for q=o(m). Total variation for unit-ball symbols is the full L1 distance of the translated normal densities, 4Phi(eta)-2; separated concentration gives eta=infinity. Smooth disjoint log-radius cutoffs of widths h_j satisfying s_m<<h_j<<u_n-u_m yield a single bounded smooth radial symbol with vanishing positive spatial derivatives, eigenvalue limits +/-1, and sqrt-index distance tending to zero. Critical alpha=2 and endpoint q=0 addressed. The archived CHECK.py was inspected; its finite quadrature is diagnostic, not proof.
